wallet_is_claimed.meaning: AtomWallet.isClaimed() is true (wallet has been claimed)
wallet_is_claimed.checkpoint: before validation of the submitted UserOp

userop_reaches_validation.meaning: a UserOp for the AtomWallet is submitted and reaches validateUserOp during the validation phase
userop_reaches_validation.checkpoint: validation phase of the submitted UserOp

warden_userop_submission_blocked.meaning: the ATOM_WARDEN is blocked from submitting UserOps on unclaimed atoms via standard bundling infrastructure (UserOp rejected at simulation by an ERC-7562-compliant bundler)
warden_userop_submission_blocked.checkpoint: after simulation of the UserOp by an ERC-7562-compliant bundler

assumptions: The UserOp is submitted for an unclaimed AtomWallet (isClaimed == false) so ownership is delegated to multiVault.getAtomWarden().
The bundler performing simulation is ERC-7562-compliant and enforces associated-storage rules during the validation phase.
The ATOM_WARDEN is the party acting on behalf of unclaimed atoms and submits UserOps through standard bundling infrastructure.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the UserOp is actually submitted in a real transaction; rejection is described as a conditional simulation outcome, so the blocked-submission effect is formalized as a potential/conditional outcome rather than an inevitable one.
Report does not specify the exact caller/actor submitting the UserOp beyond the wallet being unclaimed; the ATOM_WARDEN role is inferred from the impact statement.

limitations: The claim that all unclaimed wallets are affected is a scope generalization, not a per-transaction precondition; the plan formalizes the single-wallet scenario.
The blocked-submission effect is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report gives no numeric definition of the rejection outcome.
Code-level binding of the associated-storage rule (STO-021/STO-022) to the walletConfig.atomWarden slot read is deferred to later stages.
